video_title: Why Bitcoin’s Biggest Bears Might Be Wrong
gist: Bankless's weekly rollup (Ryan and David) contrasts Jason Calacanis's call that Bitcoin will retest the $57K June low and never make new highs with bullish targets from Willy Woo's Monte Carlo runs ($240K-$413K for a December 2028 top), Michael Nadeau ($200K-$375K), Galaxy's Alex Thorn (bottom is in) and Bitwise (base $1.6M, bull $3.6M, bear $130K by 2036), against a backdrop of 3.6% PCE, $111 oil and an ~80% Polymarket probability of a December Fed hike. The week's big story is ICE partnering with Trade XYZ to build a CFTC-regulated US venue for 24/7 perps on Hyperliquid, plus pushback from 30+ issuers against ICE/OKX tokenized stocks; they also cover Robinhood Chain's revenue collapse, Zcash dev-fund drama, Venice VVV burns, and David declining to buy the Anthropic IPO at ~$2T.

themes.theme: Bitcoin bear vs. bull price targets

insights.claim: Jason Calacanis argues Bitcoin will test the $57K June low within 12 months, that ETF outflows will continue, that it is an unproductive asset versus cash-flowing AI assets, and that it will never break its all-time high again.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis (as relayed by Bankless hosts)
insights.so_what: Prominent AI-investor bearishness frames the debate; hosts read it as a contrarian bullish signal.
insights.quote: A brutal year for Bitcoin is just getting started.

insights.claim: The hosts note Chamath has also pivoted from long-time Bitcoin bull to implying it could be hacked and go to zero due to tech vulnerabilities.
insights.speaker: Bankless co-host
insights.so_what: Sentiment among tech-investor former bulls has soured, possibly marking capitulation.

insights.claim: Willy Woo's 10,000-run Monte Carlo random-walk simulation, accounting for power-law return degradation, puts the December 2028 Bitcoin top between $240,000 and $413,000 at the 28th-50th percentile, with a range of roughly $116K to $1.4M, and a median of about $1.5M by 2034.
insights.speaker: Willy Woo (as relayed by Bankless hosts)
insights.so_what: Even conservative model outputs imply 3-5x upside by 2028, unless crypto's regime has structurally changed.

insights.claim: Galaxy's Alex Thorn effectively called the Bitcoin bottom, noting the market is 916 days into the halving cycle, past the window where every prior cycle bottomed, so a lower low than June 2026 would be unprecedented this late.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn (as relayed by Bankless hosts)
insights.so_what: Cycle-timing analysis supports adding exposure if historical patterns hold.

insights.claim: Michael Nadeau of The DeFi Report and Alex Thorn both flag the 50-week moving average, currently about $76K, as the key level Bitcoin must hold; Nadeau's cycle-top targets are $200K (bear) to about $375K (bull) with Bitcoin near $80K now.
insights.speaker: Bankless co-host
insights.so_what: A break below ~$76K would invalidate the early-bull-market thesis.

insights.claim: Bitwise's 2036 Bitcoin targets are $1.6 million base case (about 34% annual growth), $3.6 million bull case and about $130,000 bear case, derived from assigning penetration rates to gold, offshore wealth, EM currencies and sovereign reserves.
insights.speaker: Bitwise (as relayed by Bankless hosts)
insights.so_what: Long-dated targets hinge on penetration assumptions that have lagged expectations.

insights.claim: David says Bitcoin's market-penetration growth over the last two to three years has been slower than expected, consistent with a structural rerating, and that the identical four-year cycle likely won't repeat exactly.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Expect outcomes between the old cycle playbook and the bear's regime-change view.

insights.claim: Michael Saylor's Bitcoin purchases have trended down from about $130 million in the last week of September to $28M, $21M, $22M and then zero since October 19, raising the question of who the next marginal buyer is.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Loss of the largest steady buyer weakens the demand side needed to reach a $10T asset.
insights.quote: How do you take Bitcoin from a singledigit trillion dollar asset to a doubledigit trillion dollar asset?

insights.claim: Over the past two weeks Bitcoin ETFs grew about 0.5% in total AUM while ETH ETFs lost about 6%, an unusually large divergence.
insights.speaker: Bankless co-host
insights.so_what: Ether is losing relative institutional demand and needs a new narrative.

themes.theme: Macro: sticky inflation and Fed hikes

insights.claim: The FOMC held rates in a 10-2 decision, with two dissenters favoring a hike, while Polymarket prices about an 80% chance of a December rate increase.
insights.speaker: Bankless co-host
insights.so_what: A hiking bias is a headwind for risk assets including crypto.

insights.claim: September headline PCE inflation came in at 3.6% year over year, the third straight monthly acceleration (3.3% to 3.4% to 3.6%), with oil around $111 a barrel since the Iran conflict.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Rising inflation and oil keep the Fed hawkish.
insights.quote: So headline year-over-year inflation went from 3.3 to 3.4 to 3.6.

insights.claim: David warns that after next Tuesday's midterms, Trump faces no political cost to escalating the Iran war, which could push oil and inflation higher.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Post-midterm geopolitical escalation is a tail risk for oil and rates.
insights.quote: Now once the midterms are over, Trump has no cost to escalating the war in Iran.

insights.claim: Citing Michael Howell, the hosts say real inflation is higher than reported and consumer confidence, down since 2020, is the better gauge; confidence jumped to 91.7 from 81 this month, the first rise in four months, with a basic starter home around $600,000.
insights.speaker: Bankless co-host
insights.so_what: Affordability stress sits alongside high consumer spending, suggesting a K-shaped economy.

insights.claim: ICE, the parent of the New York Stock Exchange, is partnering with Trade XYZ, the largest HIP-3 deployer on Hyperliquid, to build a CFTC-regulated, KYC'd US venue for 24/7/365 perpetual futures on stocks, commodities and pre-IPO assets, pending CFTC approval.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: A major TradFi exchange operator is onboarding crypto-native perps for US retail.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid's HYPE rose about 17% on the ICE news to near all-time highs in both dollar and Bitcoin terms, about a dollar shy of its $97 dollar high.
insights.speaker: Bankless co-host
insights.so_what: Institutional validation is being priced quickly into HYPE.

insights.claim: Stanley Druckenmiller, an ICE investor, tweeted that he is an investor in Trade XYZ and will use its Hyperliquid perps, and Elon Musk replied 'interesting', prompting Trade XYZ to pitch integrating perps into X.
insights.speaker: Bankless co-host
insights.so_what: A possible X Money perps integration would give Hyperliquid mass distribution.
insights.quote: I'm excited to be an investor and trade XYZ as they partner with ICE to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on hyper liquid to the United States.

insights.claim: The hosts say the ICE deal endorses three things: perps as a crypto-pioneered product, real-world-asset price discovery on crypto rails, and non-custodial on-chain infrastructure on an EVM chain.
insights.speaker: Bankless co-host
insights.so_what: Synthetic perps are the first step toward fully tokenized assets.

insights.claim: Of about 63 companies listed as tokenized stocks by the ICE/OKX 50-50 joint venture under the SEC innovation exemption, more than 30, including Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman and Coca-Cola, asked to be delisted within the 30-day objection window after a full-page WSJ ad by the Common Sense Leadership Fund.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Onshore tokenized-stock adoption faces organized issuer resistance.
insights.quote: Attention public company CEOs, your stock, their tokens, your problem.

insights.claim: The hosts suspect incumbent rails like Nasdaq or DTC may be behind efforts to slow tokenization, but argue issuers only stand to gain more holders and liquidity, so the war is effectively won.
insights.speaker: Bankless co-host
insights.so_what: Tokenization resistance is a delaying action, not a reversal.
insights.quote: So this feels like it's just a battle, but feels like the war to me has already been won.

insights.claim: Robinhood listed a JPMorgan token on Robinhood Chain the day after JPMorgan objected, because Robinhood's offshore structure is not subject to the SEC exemption's issuer veto; David expects offshore tokenized stocks to dominate liquidity.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Issuer vetoes don't reach offshore venues, which will capture the market.

insights.claim: Hayden Adams claimed price discovery happened on-chain when Google dropped 10% while TradFi was closed; David disputes it, saying on-chain tokens were following traditional after-hours trading and liquidity is tiny, though weekend crises would send traders on-chain.
insights.speaker: David / Ryan (Bankless co-hosts)
insights.so_what: On-chain stock venues matter most for 24/7 and weekend price signals, not as primary discovery yet.

insights.claim: There are about seven different tokenized versions of Google on Uniswap trading at different prices on different chains, a fragmentation problem the hosts call untenable.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Fungibility and liquidity fragmentation must be solved for tokenized equities to scale.

themes.theme: Robinhood Chain, Zcash and token value accrual

insights.claim: Robinhood reported crypto revenue of $120 million, up 20% quarter over quarter, with Robinhood Chain contributing about $50 million, but chain revenue has collapsed to about $30,000 a day, a 99.6% decline from a peak of roughly $8.3 million a day in September.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Analysts extrapolating Q3 chain revenue will be badly wrong; on-chain data shows it in real time.

insights.claim: Vlad Tenev says Robinhood will ramp investment in Robinhood Chain's developer ecosystem after being surprised by its traction, and David expects Robinhood to spend the next 12 months trying to recapture it.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Robinhood is likely to push more on-chain activity incentives.
insights.quote: you should expect to see us ramping the investment because you just don't see growth of a new ecosystem like this.

insights.claim: Zcash routes 20% of block rewards to grants (8% to a five-person Zcash Community Grants committee and 12% to a coinholder-voted lockbox); after a ~50x price rise the fund holds about $125 million, takes in about $68 million a year versus about $6 million spent, giving 20 years of runway.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: An oversized treasury invites governance fights; proposals to end or taper the dev fund are gaining support.

insights.claim: David says a $550,000 Zcash grant to Zexy for events, five of them adult-industry conferences, triggered the controversy, with proposals ranging from Sean Bowe redirecting the 8% to the network sustainability mechanism to Zechub's soft landing wound down to zero in 2036.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Block-reward grant funding works at small scale but becomes a liability at tens of billions in market cap.
insights.quote: I think I think It works at small sizes, not at big sizes is my take.

insights.claim: Venice crossed $1 million of on-chain VVV burns in October, with burns growing about 1% a day (about 34% month over month), funded by $1/$2/$5 per subscription tier, 5% of API credits, and a discretionary monthly profit-based burn.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Revenue-linked burns are becoming the standard value-accrual model for productive tokens.

insights.claim: The hosts argue that because tokens are not equity and buybacks are non-contractual, buyback-and-burn is the only on-chain proof that a team values its token, even though early-stage companies would ideally reinvest like Amazon.
insights.speaker: Ryan / David (Bankless co-hosts)
insights.so_what: Tokens without revenue are 'basically uninvestable'; burns substitute for missing legal rights.
insights.quote: There's tokens that have no revenue which are basically uninvestable at this point in time

insights.claim: Ethena's new neobank Ethena Pay offers 12% yield on dollars via an 'Earn Plus' product built on leveraged ENA rewards, which the hosts flag as needing risk scrutiny.
insights.speaker: Bankless co-host
insights.so_what: High retail stablecoin yields carry embedded leverage risk.

themes.theme: Anthropic IPO and AI value capture

insights.claim: David notes Google search has fallen below 50% of Alphabet's revenue for the first time, from roughly 85% about four years ago, as AI erodes the internet's defining business.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: The search-ad era of the internet is ending, reshaping value capture.
insights.quote: Google search as a percent of revenue is now below 50%.

insights.claim: David is not a buyer of the Anthropic IPO at about $2 trillion because there are too many competing labs (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen), likening it to the commoditized 2021 L1 trade, unlike SpaceX which he owns because it has no second-best.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Dispersion across AI labs and possible token commoditization cap upside at mega-IPO valuations.
insights.quote: There's only one like there's no second best for SpaceX

insights.claim: David's base case is that AI tokens will be free in the future, so selling tokens may not be a great business by 2030, though the trade could run longer before a crypto-style reset.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Investors should ask what captures value once inference is commoditized.
insights.quote: my base case is that tokens are free in the future.
